prompts.title: Later with content filters
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a high-fidelity screenshot-style concept for the Later view in Tabernacle, a Firefox sidebar tab manager.
Edit target: the attached existing Domains sidebar screenshot. Transform that screen into the proposed Later screen while preserving the product's visual language. This is an illustrative concept, not a real implemented screenshot.

Composition: one straight-on portrait sidebar, approximately 960 x 1600 pixels, representing about 400 CSS pixels wide and 667 CSS pixels tall. Fill the canvas with the interface. Crisp, legible native system sans-serif type, white background, dark charcoal text, muted grey secondary text, fine grey separators, restrained 6px corners and pale grey-lavender selection. No device frame, perspective, outer presentation captions, decorative shadows or gradients. Follow the screenshot's compact practical utility aesthetic. Make the content a continuous flat list, not a stack of cards.

Header: preserve the full-width gently grey-tinted header and its proportions from the reference. Replace the globe with an outline bookmark containing a tiny clock, a recognisable Save for later symbol. Exact heading "Later" in 22 CSS px semibold, aligned with the icon. Large close X on the far right. No subtitle.
Under the header: a restrained search field with a small magnifier and exact placeholder "Search later". Margins 12 CSS px, height 32 CSS px.
Next: ONE horizontal row of four compact filter buttons reading exactly "All", "Articles", "Videos", "Documents". All is selected, pale grey-lavender fill and darker semibold text; others have quiet grey text and subtle outlines. Keep all four visible on one line; no counts on the filters, no extra category.
Next a compact count and sort strip: exact text "7 tabs" on left; exact text "Newest added" with a small downward chevron on right. A thin divider below. This sorts by when tabs were moved to Later.
The normal tab tree, folder breadcrumb, pinned-tabs strip, Domains directory and standard top search bar are replaced by this dedicated view.

Show EXACTLY SEVEN saved tab rows, top to bottom in this exact order. Each row has a recognisable small site favicon in a consistent 20px left column, a readable 14px title that can wrap to two lines, and smaller muted metadata directly underneath. Use subtle spacing to separate rows, no visible card borders. Right edge has a small grey relative-added time aligned with the metadata. Keep at least 20 CSS px clear below the final row.
1. MDN favicon; title "A practical guide to CSS container queries"; metadata "developer.mozilla.org"; time "10m ago".
2. Red YouTube play favicon; title "How the London Underground map was designed"; metadata "youtube.com · Video"; time "35m ago".
3. Blue Google Docs document favicon; title "Ideas for the next release"; metadata "docs.google.com · Document"; time "2h ago".
4. Wikipedia W favicon; title "The history of the World Wide Web"; metadata "en.wikipedia.org"; time "4h ago".
5. Red YouTube play favicon; title "Building a small desk from solid oak"; metadata "youtube.com · Video"; time "Yesterday".
6. Small black BBC favicon; title "Why we keep coming back to old technology"; metadata "bbc.co.uk"; time "Yesterday".
7. Small Google Maps pin favicon; title "Places for a weekend in Copenhagen"; metadata "maps.google.com"; time "2d ago".
Do not include thumbnails, badges, pin controls, read progress, reminders or an unread counter. The Maps entry demonstrates that All also includes tabs outside the three quick filters.
The first article row is very gently hovered with a pale neutral grey rounded background; reveal two small understated outline actions at its far right on the title line: return-to-folder icon and close X. Do not show a cursor or tooltip.

Bottom toolbar anchored to the bottom of the image, white, with a fine top divider. Preserve the existing SIX icons from the reference and ADD a new Later button between globe and history. EXACTLY SEVEN evenly spaced outline icon buttons in this order: plus, folder-plus, opposing vertical chevrons (disabled, very pale grey), globe, bookmark-with-small-clock (Later, SELECTED with the same pale grey-lavender rounded-square background as the reference selected globe), history counterclockwise clock, settings gear. The globe is now unselected. The Later icon matches the large header icon. All seven buttons clearly visible; no text labels, no badges. Consistent icon stroke weight.
Make all supplied text exact and legible. Do not add marketing copy, extra panels, explanatory annotations or fabricated product branding.
